item.title: Google Gemini adds in‑app editing for PDFs, Docs, Sheets, and more
item.description:
Google Gemini adds in‑app editing for PDFs, Docs, Sheets, and more

Google Gemini now lets users generate, preview, and edit a variety of file types without leaving the chat interface.

🔍 Overview

  • Gemini can handle PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly in a conversation.
  • The capability expands on earlier support for generating and downloading files, allowing on‑the‑fly tweaks.

🛠️ New file‑editing features

  • Edit files you generate with Gemini without exiting the app.
  • Highlight text in a file to ask Gemini questions or request changes (e.g., turn a highlighted table into a graph).
  • Expand documents to full‑screen mode for easier editing.
  • Existing Workspace integrations, such as the Gemini bar in Google Docs, continue to work.

⚙️ Supported formats & platform availability

File format Web editing Mobile editing
PDF (preview & edit) ✅ ✅
Google Docs ✅ ❌
Google Sheets ✅ ❌
Slide decks ✅ ❌
Markdown ✅ ❌
TXT ✅ ❌
Code ✅ ❌

🚀 Availability

  • The new capabilities are live today for all Gemini users.
  • PDF preview and editing are available on both web and mobile; all other formats are currently web‑only.

💡 Why it matters

  • Users no longer need to switch between Gemini and separate editing apps, streamlining workflow.
  • Full‑screen editing and contextual highlights make it easier to transform content directly within the chat.
  • Anthropic introduced a similar document‑editing feature in Claude chats earlier this year, highlighting a broader move toward integrated AI‑powered productivity tools.

#GoogleGemini #AIEditing #Productivity

Source: You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now

item.title: Google and Meta Release Frontier AI Models to Challenge OpenAI and Anthropic
item.description:
Google and Meta Release Frontier AI Models to Challenge OpenAI and Anthropic

Google and Meta have unveiled new frontier AI models that they claim match or beat the industry’s leading systems. This development marks a significant shift in the AI race, as both tech giants had previously appeared to be lagging behind the rapid advancements of OpenAI and Anthropic.

🔍 Overview

Until this week, OpenAI and Anthropic appeared to have the AI race to themselves, pulling ahead with increasingly powerful models while Google and Meta struggled to maintain pace. Google had delivered only incremental improvements since releasing Gemini 3 late last year, while Meta had yet to establish itself as a serious contender despite significant spending. This narrative upended on Monday and Tuesday with the introduction of new flagship-level models.

⚙️ Key details

Model Developer Capabilities and Attributes
Gemini 4 Argon Google Claims to match or beat flagship offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic on numerous benchmarks.
Muse Wonder Full Meta Capable of competing with GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1.
Muse Spark Meta The first major model released by Meta’s Superintelligence Labs in April.
Gemini 3 Google Formidable at launch but struggled to keep up with later models from rivals and open-weight models from China.

🧩 How it works

To reach this stage, both companies underwent significant organizational and strategic shifts:

  • Google’s Reorganization: The company moved AI-related teams out of DeepMind and into Google proper, shifting the center of gravity from London to California. This move signals a priority on commercializing AI over pure research.
  • Executive Changes: Veteran executive Jeff Dean departed to launch a new startup, and Demis Hassabis stepped back from day-to-day leadership.
  • Meta’s Investment: Meta spent billions on talent and infrastructure, including a partnership with Scale AI and its cofounder Alexandr Wang, through its new Superintelligence Labs.

🚀 Availability

Google has positioned its new model with a highly competitive pricing strategy:

  • Introductory Period: Gemini 4 Argon is currently priced at a discount of as much as 80 percent compared to its rivals per token.
  • Standard Pricing: Once the promotion ends, the model is expected to remain significantly cheaper than rival offerings.

💡 Why it matters

The arrival of these models makes the competition considerably more dynamic. Google and Meta possess deep pockets and vast product ecosystems used by billions of people—advantages that upstarts like OpenAI and Anthropic currently lack. For example, the popularity of Meta’s Muse agent assistant demonstrates the power of having a ready-made user base, despite ongoing security and privacy concerns. However, the industry faces a growing array of safety concerns and rogue AI incidents, leading to louder calls to slow development as open models continue to improve.

#GoogleGemini #MetaAI #OpenAI #GenerativeAI #AIBenchmarks

Source: The AI race is back on

item.title: Google Gemini model access shifted to paid tiers starting Oct 9
item.description:
Google Gemini model access shifted to paid tiers starting Oct 9

Starting on October 9th, Google Gemini’s free tier will be limited to the Flash Lite model.

🔍 Overview

  • Free users previously could choose Gemini Flash Lite, Flash, and Pro.
  • Access to the standard Flash model now requires a $4.99/month Google AI Plus subscription.
  • The AI Plus tier will soon lose Gemini Pro access.
  • AI Plus subscribers will be notified by email when they lose access.
  • Users can still select low, medium, or high effort levels for each model, though higher effort levels may consume usage limits faster.

⚙️ Model Access Changes

Model Required subscription Monthly price
Gemini Flash Lite Free plan —
Gemini Flash Google AI Plus $4.99
Gemini Pro / Deep Think Google AI Pro or Ultra $19.99 or $99.99

📅 Availability

  • The restriction to Flash Lite for free users begins on October 9.
  • After the change, only paid tiers will retain access to Gemini Flash and Pro models.

💡 Why it matters

  • Free users lose the ability to run higher‑performance Gemini models without paying.
  • The top‑tier Gemini Pro model and the “Deep Think” advanced reasoning option become exclusive to higher‑cost subscriptions, potentially reshaping how individuals and developers budget for AI usage.

#GoogleGemini #AIpricing #SubscriptionUpdate

Source: Google is about to remove free access to Gemini Flash and Pro

item.title: Google Gemini 3.0 Pro Detection Rates Collapse in Large Batch Processing
item.description:
Google Gemini 3.0 Pro Detection Rates Collapse in Large Batch Processing

Researchers tested the ability of Google Gemini 3.0 Pro to recover known contaminants from a corpus of 150 academic papers in the fields of medical research and supply chain management.

⚙️ Key details

The study used a contaminated corpus containing 450 injected contaminants of three types:

Contaminant Type Recovery Rate (Completed Evaluations)
Absurd out-of-context insertion 75%
Semantic reversal 50%
Typographical corruption 50%

🔍 Overview

Google Gemini 3.0 Pro was evaluated on its ability to recover a 180-contaminant answer-key subset across 60 documents. Performance varied based on the scale of the prompting regime:

  • Single document: 50% recovery
  • Small batch: 60% recovery
  • Large batch: 2.8% recovery

💡 Why it matters

Detection performance collapses at scale, with the model failing via fabrication rather than abstention. In large batches, the model produced confident findings and invented contaminants that mimicked the style of planted material—such as “quantum-powered toaster” and “telepathic squirrel”—which did not appear in any document. Additionally, plausible corruptions most likely to occur in the wild are the ones most often missed.

#GoogleGemini #LLM #AIEvaluation #DataContamination

Source: When Auditors Fabricate: Batch-Size Degradation and Confident Hallucination in LLM Detection of Planted Document Contamination

item.title: Google Releases Gemini 3.8 Flash with Enhanced Reasoning and Specialized Cyber Version
item.description:
Google Releases Gemini 3.8 Flash with Enhanced Reasoning and Specialized Cyber Version

On September 2, 2026, Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash, arriving just a few weeks after the release of its predecessor. The new model is designed to “work harder” by performing more reasoning steps on complex tasks and utilizing iterative tool calling. While it maintains the same introductory per-token pricing as Gemini 3.7 Flash, the model may incur higher total costs due to increased token usage at higher effort levels.

🔍 Overview

Gemini 3.8 Flash introduces significant improvements for software engineering and autonomous AI agents. The model is available with low, medium, and high thinking levels, allowing users to adjust performance based on task complexity. Early impressions from Artificial Analysis describe the model as the cheapest measured at its level of intelligence, despite an approximate 40% increase in total task cost driven by a 30% increase in output tokens and more turns on agentic evaluations.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Pricing: $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens.
  • Coding Performance: Aigora.ai CEO John Ennis compared its performance to Anthropic’s “Opus 5 coding quality” at a fraction of the cost, noting its speed for tasks like making remotion videos.
  • Capabilities: The model demonstrates proficiency in HTML and JavaScript, such as adding sandboxed iframe support for HTML blocks in markdown rendering tools.
  • Safeguards: Includes protections against misuse in cyber offense and Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) domains.

📊 Benchmark Results

Benchmark Performance Notes
DeepSWE v1.1 Outperforms Gemini 3.7 Flash and Anthropic’s Fable 5 in software engineering.
Vals Finance Agent V2 Outperformed competitors.
Harvey’s Legal Agent Outperformed competitors.

🛡️ Fairwind Program and Cyber Variant

Google also released Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, a specialized version available exclusively to governments and “trusted partners” through the new Fairwind Program. This program includes 650 members, such as CrowdStrike and the Center for Internet Security. Participants gain access to:

  • Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber: A model restricted to “trusted defenders.”
  • CodeMender Agent: An autonomous tool designed to find and fix vulnerabilities to protect critical infrastructure and national security.

🚀 Availability

Gemini 3.8 Flash is available now for consumers with a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, as well as developers and enterprise users. Developers who wish to minimize token usage may continue to use Gemini 3.7 Flash.

#GoogleGemini #AIagents #SoftwareEngineering #CyberSecurity

Source: Google says its new Gemini 3.8 Flash model ‘works harder’ but might cost more Source: Release: llm-gemini 0.34

item.title: Major Enterprise Software Vendors Roll Out Autonomous AI Agent Platforms in 2026
item.description:
Major Enterprise Software Vendors Roll Out Autonomous AI Agent Platforms in 2026

In 2026, enterprise AI agents are becoming a primary software investment area as businesses shift from basic chatbots to systems that understand business context, access corporate data, and execute multi-step workflows. Major vendors—including Microsoft, Salesforce, Google, ServiceNow, and SAP—are pursuing distinct platform strategies while shifting pricing away from simple flat-rate seat models toward metered consumption.

🔍 Market Shift and Pricing Complexity

As vendors transition to agentic platforms, pricing models are diversifying. Enterprises now encounter a combination of seat licenses, consumption charges, actions, credits, conversations, and AI usage units. Because each vendor meters work differently, CIOs increasingly measure cost per completed business process rather than headline license prices.

⚙️ Vendor Architectures and Pricing

The primary software providers offer distinct technical integrations and pricing structures:

Vendor Agent Technologies Pricing and Licensing Structure
Microsoft Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, Agent 365 • Microsoft 365 Copilot: $30/user/month (paid annually)
• Standalone Copilot Studio: $200/month for 25,000 Copilot Credits (requires Azure subscription)
• Pay-as-you-go pricing also available
Salesforce Agentforce, Agentforce Builder, Agent Script, Data 360, Salesforce Trust Layer • Flex Credits: $500 for 100,000 credits (standard action consumes 20 credits; voice consumes 30)
• User License: $5/user/month (requires Flex Credits)
• Conversation Pricing: $2/conversation
• Flat-fee Option: $125/user/month for some configurations
Google Gemini Enterprise, Agent Designer, Agent Development Kit • Business Edition: $21/seat/month
• Standard & Plus Editions: $30/seat/month
• Pay-as-you-go Model: No seat fee; pays for tokens, memory, compute, and storage (limited availability)
ServiceNow Enterprise workflow-native agents Built directly into existing enterprise workflows
SAP Joule Integrated directly with finance, HR, procurement, and supply-chain processes

🧩 Corporate Adoption and Results

Enterprises are already deploying these platforms to manage workflows and automate processes:

  • Atos: In June 2026, Atos deployed Microsoft 365 Copilot to 56,000 employees across 54 countries. The company is using Agent 365 to manage approximately 19,000 AI agents designed via Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry to handle internal IT, business functions, and customer deployments.
  • Tata Realty and Infrastructure: Deployed Salesforce Agentforce to manage customer engagement, reducing first-response times from days to eight hours. The deployment resulted in a 30 percent increase in lead qualification, a 10 percent rise in conversion rates, and email open rates of 50-60 percent.
  • KPMG: Achieved a 90 percent employee adoption rate of Gemini Enterprise and created more than 100 custom agents during its first month of deployment.

#EnterpriseAI #AIAgents #MicrosoftCopilot #SalesforceAgentforce #GoogleGemini

Source: Enterprise AI Agents 2026: Microsoft, Salesforce, Google, ServiceNow and SAP Pricing, Customers and Technology Compared - InfotechLead

item.title: Google partners with MrBeast for multi-year Gemini and Fitbit promotion
item.description:
Google partners with MrBeast for multi-year Gemini and Fitbit promotion

Google has signed a multi-year partnership with Jimmy “MrBeast” Donaldson, one of YouTube’s biggest creators, to promote Gemini, Google Health, and the Fitbit Air across upcoming videos.

🔍 Overview

The deal marks a significant collaboration between Google and Donaldson, whose YouTube channel became the first to hit 500 million subscribers a couple of months ago. The partnership comes amid reported efforts by YouTube to keep prominent creators exclusive to its platform.

⚙️ Key details

  • Partnership scope: Multi-year agreement featuring Gemini, Google Health, and Fitbit Air
  • First video: Scheduled for September 5
  • Format: Wilderness survival challenge with Jimmy and his crew
  • Additional promotion: Donaldson will appear in a Gemini campaign from Google

🧩 How it works

The inaugural video will follow Donaldson and his crew as they attempt to survive extreme and treacherous climates. Teams will race to navigate three unforgiving landscapes:

  • The jungle
  • The desert
  • The Arctic

According to Google, participants will use Gemini to help them identify dangers, survive brutal weather changes, and stay one step ahead. Donaldson will also use a Fitbit Air in one of his upcoming challenges.

🚀 Availability

Element Detail
First video release September 5
Featured products Gemini, Google Health, Fitbit Air
Campaign type Multi-year partnership with dedicated videos and campaign appearance

💡 Why it matters

The partnership reflects broader platform dynamics in the creator economy. A recent Bloomberg report noted that YouTube has been offering prominent creators deals to keep their content exclusive to its site as more creators strike deals with Netflix.

#MrBeast #GoogleGemini #Fitbit #YouTube #AIpartnerships #creatoreconomy

Source: Google is sending MrBeast into the wilderness, armed with AI
